source.author: verg
source.text: O Regina, novam cui condere Iuppiter urbem iustitiaque dedit gentis frenare superbas, Troes te miseri, ventis maria omnia vecti, oramus, prohibe infandos a navibus ignis, parce pio generi, et propius res aspice nostras.
source.text_original: 'O Regina, novam cui condere Iuppiter urbem / iustitiaque dedit gentis frenare superbas, / Troes te miseri, ventis maria omnia vecti, / oramus, prohibe infandos a navibus ignis, / parce pio generi, et propius res aspice nostras.
source.text_english: O Queen, to whom Jupiter has granted to found a new city and with justice to curb proud nations, we wretched Trojans, borne by the winds over all seas, pray you: keep the accursed fires away from our ships, spare a pious race, and look more closely upon our fortunes.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Haemoniam primis Pelias frenabat ab annis, iam gravis et longus populis metus: illius amnes Ionium quicumque petunt, ille Othryn et Haemum atque imum felix versabat vomere Olympum.
reuse.text_original: Haemoniam primis Pelias frenabat ab annis, / iam gravis et longus populis metus: illius amnes / Ionium quicumque petunt, ille Othryn et Haemum / atque imum felix versabat vomere Olympum.
reuse.text_english: From his earliest years Pelias was restraining Haemonia, now a heavy and long-standing fear to the peoples: for all its rivers that seek the Ionian Sea, he ploughed Othrys and Haemus and even the lowliest slopes of Olympus with his happy plow.
